questions.question: What is urbanisation?
options: Growth and expansion of towns and cities
Movement from towns to forests only
questions.answer: Growth and expansion of towns and cities
questions.explanation: Urbanisation is the growth of towns and cities as more people settle in them.

questions.question: Which settlement is more likely to have many industries and large commercial centres?
questions.explanation: Towns and cities concentrate industries, shops and services.

questions.question: Why do many people settle in areas with fertile soils?
questions.explanation: Fertile soil grows good crops, so people settle where food can be produced.

questions.question: Why are settlements often found near water sources?
options: People need water for domestic and economic activities
questions.answer: People need water for domestic and economic activities
questions.explanation: Water is needed for drinking, washing, animals and crops.

questions.question: What problem can rapid urbanisation create?
options: Pressure on housing and social services
questions.answer: Pressure on housing and social services
questions.explanation: When towns grow faster than their services, housing, water and schools fall short.

questions.question: A town has many factories, schools, hospitals and shops. What is likely to attract people to the town?
questions.explanation: Jobs and services are the main pull factors that draw people to towns.

questions.question: Which factor can encourage settlement in an area?
questions.explanation: People settle where they can get water, food, work and safety.

questions.question: Why do many people prefer to settle near fertile land?
questions.explanation: Fertile land grows good crops, so families can feed themselves and sell surplus.

questions.question: Which is a possible effect of rural-urban migration?
questions.explanation: More arrivals than housing leads to crowding and slums.

questions.question: Which settlement is most likely to have a large number of commercial activities?
questions.explanation: Towns concentrate shops, markets and businesses.

questions.question: Why do roads influence settlement?
questions.explanation: People settle where they can travel to markets, schools and work.

questions.question: Which historical activity contributed to the growth of towns?
questions.explanation: Places where people came to buy and sell grew into towns.

questions.question: Why did some early settlements grow near trading centres?
options: Trade created opportunities for exchange and employment
Trading centres had no economic activity
questions.answer: Trade created opportunities for exchange and employment
questions.explanation: Where goods change hands there is work, income and reason to settle.

questions.question: Which soil type is generally suitable for growing many crops because it contains a mixture of soil particles?
questions.explanation: Loam mixes sand, silt and clay, so it holds both water and plant food.

questions.question: Which farming practice helps reduce soil erosion on sloping land?
questions.explanation: Ploughing along the contour slows water running down the slope.

questions.question: What is soil erosion?
options: Removal of the top fertile layer of soil
questions.answer: Removal of the top fertile layer of soil
questions.explanation: Soil erosion is the wearing away of the fertile top layer by water or wind.

questions.question: Which of the following can cause soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Removing trees leaves soil bare, so rain washes it away.

questions.question: What is terracing mainly used for?
questions.explanation: Terraces are steps cut across a slope that slow running water.

questions.question: Which activity is likely to increase soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Bare steep ground lets rainwater run fast and wash the soil away.

questions.question: Which part of the soil contains most of the organic matter useful to plants?
questions.explanation: Topsoil is the dark upper layer rich in decayed plant and animal matter.

questions.question: Why is topsoil important?
options: It contains nutrients needed by many plants
It is always made of rocks
questions.answer: It contains nutrients needed by many plants
questions.explanation: Topsoil holds the plant food and moisture that crops need.

questions.question: Which farming practice helps control soil erosion on steep slopes?
questions.explanation: Terraces are steps cut across a slope that slow water running downhill.

questions.question: Why should farmers avoid cultivating very steep slopes without conservation measures?
options: They are highly prone to soil erosion
questions.answer: They are highly prone to soil erosion
questions.explanation: Water runs fast down steep ground and carries the soil with it.

questions.question: Which practice is most likely to improve soil fertility?
questions.explanation: Manure adds nutrients and improves the structure of the soil.

questions.question: Why should farmers conserve soil?
options: To maintain soil fertility and agricultural productivity
questions.answer: To maintain soil fertility and agricultural productivity
questions.explanation: Healthy soil keeps producing good harvests season after season.

questions.question: Which activity can lead to loss of fertile topsoil?
questions.explanation: Removing trees leaves soil bare so rain washes the topsoil away.

questions.question: Which activity can cause soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Bare soil has nothing to hold it, so rain and wind carry it away.

questions.question: A farmer plants grass on a bare slope. What problem is the farmer mainly trying to control?
questions.explanation: Grass roots bind the soil and slow water running down the slope.

questions.question: Which practice helps prevent soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Terraces are steps cut across a slope that slow running water.

questions.question: Which agent commonly causes soil erosion in Uganda?
questions.explanation: Rainwater running over the surface is the main cause of erosion in Uganda.

Fan-shaped land formed where a river enters a lake or sea
A person who travels to an unknown place to find out about it
The movement of skilled people out of a country to work elsewhere
questions.answer: A large group of people sharing origin, language family and customs

An area set aside by government for protecting wild animals
A smaller group within an ethnic group sharing one language and culture

questions.question: What is trade?
options: Buying and selling goods and services
questions.answer: Buying and selling goods and services
questions.explanation: Trade is the exchange of goods and services, usually for money.

questions.question: Trade carried out within a country is called:
questions.explanation: Internal trade takes place inside the borders of one country.

questions.question: Trade between two or more countries is called:
questions.explanation: International trade crosses national borders.

questions.question: What is an export?
options: A good brought into a country
A good sent out of a country for sale
A good destroyed in a country
questions.answer: A good sent out of a country for sale
questions.explanation: Exports are goods sold to other countries.

questions.question: What is an import?
options: A good brought into a country for sale or use
A good sent out of a country
questions.answer: A good brought into a country for sale or use
questions.explanation: Imports are goods bought from other countries.

questions.question: Which of the following can Uganda export?
questions.explanation: Coffee is one of Uganda's main export earners.

questions.question: Why is regional trade important?
options: It allows countries to exchange goods and services
questions.answer: It allows countries to exchange goods and services
questions.explanation: Each country sells what it produces well and buys what it lacks.

questions.question: A Ugandan trader buys goods from Kenya and sells them in Uganda. What type of trade is this?
questions.explanation: The goods crossed a national border, so this is international trade.

questions.question: Why are cash crops important to Uganda?
options: They can earn income and foreign exchange
questions.answer: They can earn income and foreign exchange
questions.explanation: Selling cash crops abroad brings foreign currency into the country.

questions.question: Which transport problem can increase the price of goods?
questions.explanation: Traders add the cost of moving goods to the selling price.

questions.question: What is internal trade?
options: Trade carried out within a country
questions.answer: Trade carried out within a country
questions.explanation: Internal trade takes place inside the borders of one country.

questions.question: What is international trade?
questions.explanation: International trade crosses national borders.

questions.question: A Ugandan company sells coffee to another country. What is the coffee called from Uganda's point of view?
questions.explanation: Goods sold out of the country are exports.

questions.question: Uganda buys machinery from another country. The machinery is an:
questions.explanation: Goods bought from abroad are imports.

questions.question: Why are exports important?
questions.explanation: Selling abroad brings foreign currency needed to pay for imports.

questions.question: Which service helps traders safely keep and transfer money?
questions.explanation: Banks keep money safe and move it between people and businesses.

questions.question: Which activity involves buying and selling goods?
questions.explanation: Trade is the exchange of goods and services, usually for money.

questions.question: Which person buys goods for personal use?
questions.explanation: A consumer is the person who finally uses the goods.

questions.question: Which person or organisation makes goods?
questions.explanation: A producer grows or manufactures the goods that others buy.

questions.question: Why do traders need markets?
options: Markets provide places where goods can be bought and sold
questions.answer: Markets provide places where goods can be bought and sold
questions.explanation: A market brings buyers and sellers together in one place.

questions.question: Which means of transport is most suitable for moving bulky goods over long distances by land?
questions.explanation: Lorries on roads can carry heavy loads far inland.

questions.question: Which transport uses railway lines?
questions.explanation: Trains run on railway lines.

questions.question: Which means of transport is generally the fastest for long-distance international travel?
questions.explanation: Aircraft cover long distances far faster than any land or water transport.

questions.question: What is one advantage of water transport?
options: It is always faster than aircraft
questions.explanation: Ships and ferries carry heavy, bulky cargo cheaply.

questions.question: Which means of transport is most suitable for crossing a lake?
questions.explanation: Boats and ferries are the practical way to cross a lake.

questions.question: Which means of transport is particularly useful for transporting passengers over very long distances quickly?
questions.explanation: Aircraft cover very long distances in a few hours.

questions.question: Why are roads important to farmers?
options: They help farmers transport produce to markets
They prevent farmers from selling produce
questions.answer: They help farmers transport produce to markets
questions.explanation: Without a usable road, produce cannot reach buyers in time.

questions.question: Which transport problem can make agricultural products spoil before reaching markets?
questions.explanation: Slow journeys on bad roads let perishable produce rot before it is sold.

questions.question: Why is good transport important for national development?
options: It connects producers, consumers and markets
questions.answer: It connects producers, consumers and markets
questions.explanation: Goods, workers and services can only move where transport allows.

questions.question: Which means of transport is generally suitable for transporting large quantities of heavy goods over long distances?
questions.explanation: Trains carry very heavy, bulky loads cheaply over long land distances.

questions.question: A farmer has harvested a large quantity of maize and needs to take it to a distant market. Which service is most important?
questions.explanation: Produce cannot be sold until it can be moved to where buyers are.

questions.question: Which transport method is useful for moving bulky goods over long distances?
questions.explanation: Trains carry very heavy, bulky loads cheaply over long distances.

questions.question: Why is air transport useful for urgent goods?
questions.explanation: Aircraft deliver perishable or urgent goods in hours rather than days.

questions.question: Which means of transport is used on Lake Victoria?
questions.explanation: Boats and ferries carry people and goods across the lake.

questions.question: Why are good roads important to traders?
options: They make movement of goods easier
questions.answer: They make movement of goods easier
questions.explanation: Good roads let goods reach markets quickly and in good condition.

questions.question: Who were missionaries?
options: People who travelled to spread their religion and provide related services
People who came only to trade gold
People who came only to hunt
People who built every railway in Africa
questions.answer: People who travelled to spread their religion and provide related services
questions.explanation: Missionaries came to spread their faith and also started schools and health centres.

questions.question: Which group played an important role in spreading Islam in East Africa?
questions.explanation: Arab traders reaching the coast and interior spread Islam alongside their trade.

questions.question: Why did some European explorers travel through Africa?
options: To explore and obtain geographical information
questions.answer: To explore and obtain geographical information
questions.explanation: Explorers mapped rivers, lakes and land and reported back to Europe.

questions.question: Why did missionaries establish schools in some parts of Uganda?
options: To provide education and support the spread of their religious teachings
questions.answer: To provide education and support the spread of their religious teachings
questions.explanation: Missionaries taught reading and writing partly so people could read religious books.

questions.question: Why did traders come to East Africa?
questions.explanation: Traders came seeking goods such as ivory, and brought items to sell in exchange.

questions.question: Which group played an important role in the early spread of Islam along the East African coast?
questions.explanation: Arab traders settled along the coast and, with the Swahili, spread Islam there.

questions.question: Which group played a major role in spreading Islam along the East African coast?
questions.explanation: Arab traders settled along the coast and spread Islam there.

questions.question: Why did traders visit the East African coast?
questions.explanation: Traders came for goods such as ivory and brought items to sell in exchange.

questions.question: Why should Ugandans learn about their country's history?
options: To understand their past and help shape the future
questions.answer: To understand their past and help shape the future
questions.explanation: Knowing how the country came to be helps citizens make better decisions now.

questions.question: Why is history important?
options: It helps people understand events of the past
questions.answer: It helps people understand events of the past
questions.explanation: Understanding the past helps explain the present and guide the future.

questions.question: Which group played an important role in the spread of Christianity in many parts of Uganda?
questions.explanation: Missionaries came to teach their faith and founded churches and schools.

questions.question: Why did missionaries establish schools?
options: To provide education alongside their missionary work
questions.answer: To provide education alongside their missionary work
questions.explanation: Reading was needed for religious study, so missionaries taught it in schools.

questions.question: Which of the following is a source of historical information?
questions.explanation: Oral tradition, documents and artefacts are all sources of history.

questions.question: Which source can provide written information about the past?
questions.explanation: Letters, records and books written in the past are historical documents.

questions.question: Why should historical information be checked carefully?
options: Some information may be inaccurate or biased
All historical information is automatically correct
questions.answer: Some information may be inaccurate or biased
questions.explanation: Different sources may disagree, so a historian compares them before believing one.

questions.question: Which activity helped connect inland Uganda to the coast during colonial times?
questions.explanation: The Uganda Railway linked the interior to the coast at Mombasa.

questions.question: What is vegetation?
options: Plants growing naturally in an area
questions.answer: Plants growing naturally in an area
questions.explanation: Vegetation means the plant cover growing naturally in an area.

questions.question: Which human activity can destroy natural vegetation?
questions.explanation: Deforestation removes trees and destroys the natural plant cover.

questions.question: Which natural vegetation is associated with areas receiving enough rainfall?
questions.explanation: Plenty of rainfall supports thick tree growth, so forests develop.

questions.question: Which human activity threatens natural vegetation?
questions.explanation: Deforestation removes trees and destroys the natural plant cover.

questions.question: Why is vegetation important to wildlife?
questions.explanation: Plants feed many animals and give them places to hide and nest.

questions.question: Which vegetation type is commonly associated with areas having moderate rainfall and long grass?
questions.explanation: Moderate rainfall supports grassland with tall grass and scattered trees.

questions.question: What is meant by “Vegetation”?

Being held in custody, often without trial
All the plants growing in an area
